executive_assessment.text: Turkana evidence differentiates livelihood and gender vulnerabilities and identifies resource/coordination barriers. It is dated May 2023, not a current county risk ranking.
Sarima shows historical energy-project benefit and water-service tensions; Samburu and pastoral-service networks add governance capacities, with no independent outcome evaluation.

geographic_notes.text: Turkana's May 2023 county assessment describes drought, floods, intense rainfall and unreliable seasons affecting pastoral, farming, fishing and water-dependent livelihoods.
Turkana's May 2023 county assessment describes drought and heat reducing pasture and water and increasing grazing competition and the likelihood of insecurity.
The May 2023 Turkana assessment describes women and girls traveling far for riverbed water and higher drought-related malnutrition risks for pregnant/lactating women, children and older people.

The May 2023 Turkana assessment identifies inadequate resources and poor institutional coordination as adaptation barriers; it describes community action groups as a resource-management capacity, without evaluating outcomes.

International Alert's February 2026 publisher summary describes drought, floods and resource pressures amplifying competition among pastoral, agropastoral and fishing communities in Marsabit and Turkana.

International Alert's February 2026 summary describes unequal land/water access, movement and conservation restrictions as livelihood and tension mediators, and recommends inclusive conflict-sensitive programming.
A 2023 structured review describes drought-related pasture and water stress alongside resource-related raids in Turkana, Samburu and Marsabit, while emphasizing contested and varying mechanisms.

The 2023 review describes historical wind-park job disputes between Turkana and Samburu in Sarima and a failed borehole desalination unit; these illustrate project-benefit and service risks, not proof that climate hazards caused violence.
At publication in 2023, the review described oil-site roadblocks and attacks over water and employment, alongside prospective production risks; this is not an update on 2026 oil operations.
Saferworld reports supporting a Samburu rangeland-access legislative process during 2018-2022, alongside a peace/cohesion forum; institutional outputs do not establish reduced conflict.

ACIAR's July 2023 publisher summary recommends recognizing local pastoral-service networks in Isiolo and Marsabit, including herders, herd owners, animal-health providers, mobile-money services and brokers.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 17 of 17 evidence records and 2 of 2 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The World Bank CCDR PDF could not be opened in this collection workflow; no CCDR-based claims are included.

National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
Government-described resource-conflict mechanism has no event-specific causal estimate.
The most detailed subnational hazard and gender evidence located is Turkana's 2023 county assessment; no newer comparable county assessment was added for Marsabit or Samburu.
International Alert and ACIAR full reports were not inspected, so related claims remain limited to publisher summaries.
Conflict-related constraints on adaptation are mostly synthesized from literature or program descriptions; independent current evaluation evidence remains limited.
No present-day county conflict prevalence is inferred from the 2023 Turkana assessment or historical energy-project cases.
The strongest new direct mechanism is locally reported resource competition; implementer descriptions and recommendations are not independent outcome evidence.
